resources.label: Grokking the Low Level Design Interview

children.title: Extending the design
children.description: Expect a follow-up that adds a requirement. A clean design absorbs it with a new class, not edits across many.

leetcode-patterns.title: How to Practice: Method, Tracking, and Review
leetcode-patterns.description: Build a practice system before you grind. You will set a weekly plan, log every attempt, and review failures so each problem teaches a pattern instead of a one-off answer.
topics: Easy, medium and hard: how to sequence them
The 20-minute rule before looking at a hint
leetcode-patterns.challenge: Set up your tracker and plan a 4-week schedule. Solve 5 easy problems and log the pattern, time and mistakes for each.

children.title: Easy, medium and hard in order
children.description: Start with easy problems to learn the patterns, then mediums on the same pattern, and hards last. Jumping to hards early only teaches frustration.

children.title: Curated lists
children.description: Pick one list such as Grind 75 or the NeetCode roadmap and finish it. Switching lists every week gives you breadth but no depth.

children.title: The 20-minute rule
children.description: Spend about 20 minutes on your own, then read a hint, then the solution. After reading, close it and solve the problem again from scratch.

resources.label: Tech Interview Handbook - Coding interview study plan

children.title: Avoiding the memorize trap
children.description: Memorized solutions fail on the first variation. After each problem, write down the pattern, the signal that told you to use it, and what would change it.

resources.label: Tech Interview Handbook - Coding interview study plan

children.title: Logging attempts and mistakes
children.description: Record the date, time taken, pattern and the exact mistake. Your own mistake log shows which patterns need work.

resources.label: Tech Interview Handbook - Coding interview study plan

children.title: Spaced repetition
children.description: Re-solve a problem after a day, a week and a month. Retrieval after a gap is what makes a pattern stick.

children.title: Pattern notes
children.description: For each pattern keep a short template, its signal words, its time and space cost, and two problems that use it.

children.title: Reviewing weak patterns
children.description: Once a week, pick the pattern with the most mistakes in your log and do three fresh problems on it.

resources.label: Tech Interview Handbook - Coding interview study plan

leetcode-patterns.title: Arrays and Hashing Patterns
leetcode-patterns.description: Drill the highest-frequency interview patterns. You will solve duplicate, anagram, grouping and prefix-sum problems until the hash map reflex is automatic.
topics: Group Anagrams and Top K Frequent
leetcode-patterns.challenge: Solve 10 array and hashing problems. Explain the shared pattern across any three of them in your own words.

children.title: Contains Duplicate and Two Sum
children.description: A set answers "seen before?" in constant time, and a map from value to index turns Two Sum from quadratic into one pass.

children.title: Group Anagrams and Top K Frequent
children.description: Use a canonical key such as sorted letters or a count tuple to group items. Bucket by frequency to avoid a full sort.

children.title: Product of Array Except Self
children.description: Build a prefix product going right and a suffix product going left. No division is needed, and you can reuse the output array.

resources.label: LeetCode - Product of Array Except Self

children.title: Subarray Sum Equals K
children.description: Store counts of each prefix sum. A subarray sums to k when the current prefix minus k was seen before.

children.title: Longest Consecutive Sequence
children.description: Put numbers in a set and only start counting from a number that has no predecessor. Each element is visited once, giving linear time.

children.title: Valid Anagram
children.description: Compare character counts instead of sorting. A fixed-size array is enough when the alphabet is small.

children.title: Valid Sudoku
children.description: Track what you have seen per row, column and box with sets. The box index is row divided by 3 and column divided by 3.

children.title: Choosing the key
children.description: Most hashing problems come down to picking the right key. Ask what two items must share to count as the same.

leetcode-patterns.title: Two Pointers and Sliding Window Patterns
leetcode-patterns.description: Drill linear-time techniques for sorted data and substrings. You will recognize when a window or a pair of pointers replaces a nested loop.
topics: Valid Palindrome and Two Sum II
Best Time to Buy and Sell Stock
leetcode-patterns.challenge: Solve 10 problems. For each, write down the signal in the statement that told you to use a window or two pointers.

children.title: Valid Palindrome and Two Sum II
children.description: On sorted or symmetric data, start at both ends and move the pointer that can improve the answer.

children.title: 3Sum and Container With Most Water
children.description: Sort, fix one value and run two pointers on the rest, skipping duplicates. For the container, move the shorter wall inward.

children.title: Best Time to Buy and Sell Stock
children.description: Track the lowest price so far and the best profit as you scan. It is a window whose left edge jumps to a new low.

resources.label: LeetCode - Best Time to Buy and Sell Stock

children.title: Longest Substring Without Repeating Characters
children.description: Grow the right edge, and when a repeat appears move the left edge past it. A map of last positions makes the jump direct.

resources.label: LeetCode - Longest Substring Without Repeating Characters

children.title: Minimum Window Substring
children.description: Count what you need, expand until the window is valid, then shrink from the left while it stays valid, recording the best.

children.title: Sliding Window Maximum
children.description: Keep a deque of indices whose values decrease. The front is always the maximum, and you drop indices that leave the window.

children.title: Signals for two pointers
children.description: Sorted input, a pair or triple target, or in-place rearranging usually points to two pointers.

children.title: Signals for a window
children.description: A contiguous subarray or substring with a constraint, asking for the longest, shortest or count, suggests a window.

leetcode-patterns.title: Stack, Queue, and Monotonic Patterns
leetcode-patterns.description: Drill problems where order of arrival matters. You will use stacks for matching and nearest-greater problems, and queues for level-by-level work.
leetcode-patterns.challenge: Solve 8 problems, including 2 monotonic stack problems. Draw the stack state step by step for one of them.

children.title: Valid Parentheses and Min Stack
children.description: A stack matches the most recent opener first. Store the running minimum next to each value to answer min in constant time.

children.title: Evaluate Reverse Polish Notation
children.description: Push numbers, and on an operator pop two operands and push the result. Watch the order for subtraction and division.

children.title: Daily Temperatures
children.description: Keep a stack of indices with decreasing temperatures. When a warmer day arrives, pop and record the distance.

resources.label: Tech Interview Handbook - Coding interview study plan

children.title: Next Greater Element
children.description: Store each element's answer when it is popped by a larger value. Each element is pushed and popped once, so it is linear.

children.title: Largest Rectangle in Histogram
children.description: A bar's rectangle extends to the nearest shorter bar on each side. A stack of increasing heights finds both edges in one pass.

children.title: Car Fleet
children.description: Sort by position, compute arrival times, and use a stack where a slower car ahead absorbs those behind it.

children.title: Generate Parentheses
children.description: Build strings while tracking open and close counts. Only add a close when it would not exceed the opens.

children.title: Recursion as a stack
children.description: The call stack is a stack. Any recursive solution can be written with an explicit stack when depth is a concern.

resources.label: Tech Interview Handbook - Coding interview study plan

leetcode-patterns.title: Binary Search Patterns
leetcode-patterns.description: Drill binary search beyond sorted arrays. You will search rotated arrays and search on the answer space, with careful boundary handling.
topics: Binary Search and Search Insert Position
Find Minimum in Rotated Sorted Array
leetcode-patterns.challenge: Solve 8 problems. Write one reusable binary search template and note exactly where off-by-one errors appear.

children.title: Binary Search and Search Insert Position
children.description: Keep a range that must contain the answer and halve it. The insert position is where the left pointer ends up.

children.title: Avoiding off-by-one errors
children.description: Choose one convention, such as a half-open range, and keep it. Compute the middle as left plus half the distance.

resources.label: Tech Interview Handbook - Coding interview study plan

children.title: Search in Rotated Sorted Array
children.description: At each step one half is sorted. Check whether the target lies in the sorted half, and go there or to the other half.

resources.label: LeetCode - Search in Rotated Sorted Array

children.title: Find Minimum in Rotated Sorted Array
children.description: Compare the middle to the right end. If the middle is larger, the minimum is to its right.

resources.label: LeetCode - Find Minimum in Rotated Sorted Array

children.title: Koko Eating Bananas
children.description: When the answer is a number and you can check a guess quickly, binary search over the range of answers.

children.title: Time Based Key-Value Store
children.description: Store timestamps in increasing order per key and binary search for the latest one at or before the query.

children.title: Median of Two Sorted Arrays
children.description: Binary search the cut position in the smaller array so the left halves together hold half the elements.

resources.label: LeetCode - Median of Two Sorted Arrays

children.title: Recognizing monotonic checks
children.description: If a yes or no check flips only once as the input grows, binary search applies even when nothing is sorted.

leetcode-patterns.title: Linked List Patterns
leetcode-patterns.description: Drill pointer manipulation. You will reverse, merge and reorder lists, and detect cycles with fast and slow pointers.
topics: Linked List Cycle and Cycle II
Reorder List and Remove Nth Node From End
LRU Cache and Copy List With Random Pointer
leetcode-patterns.challenge: Solve 8 problems. Implement LRU Cache with a hash map and a doubly linked list, and explain why both are needed.

children.title: Reverse Linked List
children.description: Walk the list and flip each next pointer, keeping the previous node. Save next before you overwrite it.

children.title: Merge Two Sorted Lists
children.description: Use a dummy head and attach the smaller node each step. The dummy avoids special cases for the first node.

children.title: Linked List Cycle and Cycle II
children.description: A fast pointer moves two steps and a slow one moves one. They meet if there is a cycle, and a second pass finds its start.

children.title: Finding the middle
children.description: When the fast pointer reaches the end, the slow one is at the middle. This is the first step in many list problems.

children.title: Reorder List and Remove Nth Node From End
children.description: Find the middle, reverse the second half and merge. For the nth node, space two pointers n apart.

resources.label: LeetCode - Remove Nth Node From End of List

children.title: Add Two Numbers
children.description: Walk both lists with a carry and build the result. Handle different lengths and a final carry.

children.title: LRU Cache
children.description: Pair a hash map with a doubly linked list so lookup and move-to-front are both constant time.

children.title: Copy List With Random Pointer
children.description: Map each original node to its copy, then wire up next and random in a second pass. Or interleave copies to save space.

resources.label: LeetCode - Copy List with Random Pointer

leetcode-patterns.title: Tree Patterns: DFS and BFS
leetcode-patterns.description: Drill tree problems. You will choose between depth-first and breadth-first traversals and pass information up or down the recursion.
topics: Invert Binary Tree and Maximum Depth
Same Tree, Subtree and Balanced Tree
Level Order Traversal and Right Side View
Validate BST and Kth Smallest in BST
Binary Tree Maximum Path Sum and Serialize/Deserialize
leetcode-patterns.challenge: Solve 12 tree problems. Group them into 'return a value up' versus 'carry state down' and note the template for each.

children.title: Invert Binary Tree and Maximum Depth
children.description: Many tree problems are solved by trusting recursion: solve the children, then combine at the node.

resources.label: LeetCode - Maximum Depth of Binary Tree

children.title: Same Tree, Subtree and Balanced Tree
children.description: Compare two trees node by node. Balanced Tree returns height and a flag together to avoid repeated work.

children.title: Level Order Traversal
children.description: Use a queue and process one level at a time by counting how many nodes are in the queue at the start of each round.

resources.label: LeetCode - Binary Tree Level Order Traversal

children.title: Right Side View
children.description: Take the last node of each level, or do a depth-first walk that visits the right child first.

resources.label: LeetCode - Binary Tree Right Side View

children.title: Lowest Common Ancestor
children.description: If the two targets are found in different subtrees, the current node is the answer. In a search tree, compare values to go left or right.

resources.label: LeetCode - Lowest Common Ancestor of a Binary Tree

children.title: Validate BST and Kth Smallest
children.description: Pass down the allowed range for validation. An in-order walk visits search tree values in sorted order.

resources.label: LeetCode - Kth Smallest Element in a BST

children.title: Binary Tree Maximum Path Sum
children.description: Return the best downward path from each node, but update a global best using both children. Ignore negative branches.

resources.label: LeetCode - Binary Tree Maximum Path Sum

children.title: Serialize and Deserialize
children.description: Write the tree in pre-order with markers for empty nodes. Reading it back uses the same order.

resources.label: LeetCode - Serialize and Deserialize Binary Tree

leetcode-patterns.title: Heap and Priority Queue Patterns
leetcode-patterns.description: Drill problems that ask for the best k items or a running middle. You will pick min-heaps or max-heaps and keep heap sizes bounded.
topics: Kth Largest Element in a Stream
Last Stone Weight and K Closest Points
leetcode-patterns.challenge: Solve 8 problems. Explain why a size-k min-heap beats sorting for top-k, with the Big-O for both.

children.title: Kth Largest Element in a Stream
children.description: Keep a min-heap of size k. Its top is always the kth largest seen so far.

resources.label: LeetCode - Kth Largest Element in a Stream

children.title: Last Stone Weight
children.description: Repeatedly take the two largest values. A max-heap does that in logarithmic time per step.

children.title: K Closest Points to Origin
children.description: Keep a heap of size k keyed by distance. Compare squared distances to avoid square roots.

resources.label: LeetCode - K Closest Points to Origin

children.title: Top K Frequent Elements
children.description: Count with a map, then use a size-k heap or bucket by frequency for linear time.

children.title: Task Scheduler
children.description: Always run the most frequent remaining task, and use a cooldown queue. A counting formula gives the same answer.

children.title: Merge K Sorted Lists
children.description: Put the head of each list in a min-heap, pop the smallest and push its next node.

children.title: Find Median from Data Stream
children.description: Keep a max-heap for the lower half and a min-heap for the upper half, balanced in size. The median is at the tops.

resources.label: LeetCode - Find Median from Data Stream

children.title: When to use a heap
children.description: Reach for a heap when you repeatedly need the smallest or largest item from a changing set.

leetcode-patterns.title: Backtracking Patterns
leetcode-patterns.description: Drill search over choices. You will generate subsets, permutations and combinations, and prune branches early to stay inside the time limit.
topics: Letter Combinations of a Phone Number
leetcode-patterns.challenge: Solve 8 problems with one shared backtracking template. Mark where each one prunes and how much that saves.

children.title: Subsets and Subsets II
children.description: For each element choose to include it or not. Sort and skip equal neighbors at the same depth to avoid duplicates.

children.title: Permutations
children.description: Build one position at a time, using a used marker or swapping in place. Undo the choice after the recursive call.

children.title: Combination Sum
children.description: Recurse with a remaining target and a start index so the same combination is not built in different orders.

children.title: Word Search
children.description: Depth-first search on a grid, marking the current cell as visited and restoring it when you return.

children.title: Palindrome Partitioning
children.description: At each position try every prefix that is a palindrome and recurse on the rest. Precompute palindromes to speed it up.

children.title: Letter Combinations of a Phone Number
children.description: Each digit maps to letters. Choose one per digit and build the string as you go.

resources.label: LeetCode - Letter Combinations of a Phone Number

children.title: N-Queens
children.description: Track used columns and both diagonals in sets. Place a queen row by row and backtrack when a row has no safe cell.

children.title: Choose, explore, undo
children.description: Every backtracking solution has the same three steps. Pruning early cuts the search tree most.

resources.label: Tech Interview Handbook - Coding interview study plan

leetcode-patterns.title: Graph Patterns: BFS, DFS, and Union-Find
leetcode-patterns.description: Drill graph problems, including grids. You will count islands, order dependencies and group connected components.
topics: Number of Islands and Max Area of Island
Number of Connected Components and Graph Valid Tree
leetcode-patterns.challenge: Solve 10 graph problems. For each, write what the nodes and edges are, because that is the hardest step.

children.title: Number of Islands and Max Area of Island
children.description: Scan the grid and start a search at each unvisited land cell, marking cells as you visit them. Count starts or track area.

children.title: Pacific Atlantic Water Flow
children.description: Search backward from each ocean's border to find cells that can reach it, then intersect the two sets.

children.title: Clone Graph and Rotting Oranges
children.description: Clone with a map from old node to new node. For oranges, start BFS from all rotten ones and count levels.

children.title: Word Ladder
children.description: Treat words as nodes and one-letter changes as edges. BFS gives the shortest sequence length.

children.title: Course Schedule I and II
children.description: Detect a cycle in a directed graph. Topological sort with in-degree counts also gives a valid order.

children.title: Topological sort
children.description: Repeatedly take nodes with no incoming edges. If you cannot take all of them, there is a cycle.

children.title: Connected Components and Valid Tree
children.description: Union the endpoints of each edge. A tree has n-1 edges and no edge joins nodes already connected.

resources.label: LeetCode - Number of Connected Components in an Undirected Graph

children.title: Union-find with path compression
children.description: Find with path compression and union by rank give near-constant time. It suits problems that merge groups over time.

leetcode-patterns.title: Shortest Path and Advanced Graph Patterns
leetcode-patterns.description: Drill weighted graph problems. You will choose Dijkstra, Bellman-Ford or a minimum spanning tree based on the constraints.
topics: Min Cost to Connect All Points
leetcode-patterns.challenge: Solve 6 problems. Write a decision table: which algorithm for which graph property, with an example for each.

children.title: Network Delay Time
children.description: Run Dijkstra from the source with a min-heap. The answer is the largest shortest distance, or -1 if some node is unreachable.

children.title: Cheapest Flights Within K Stops
children.description: Limit the number of edges. Bellman-Ford with k+1 rounds, or BFS with a stop count, handles the constraint.

resources.label: LeetCode - Cheapest Flights Within K Stops

children.title: Path With Minimum Effort
children.description: The cost of a path is its worst step, not the sum. Dijkstra works with max as the combine rule, or binary search the answer.

children.title: Swim in Rising Water
children.description: Again the cost is the largest value on the path. Use a heap that always expands the lowest-cost frontier cell.

children.title: Min Cost to Connect All Points
children.description: Connect all points at the lowest total cost. Prim's with a heap or Kruskal's with union-find both work.

resources.label: LeetCode - Min Cost to Connect All Points

children.title: Prim's and Kruskal's
children.description: Prim's grows one tree from a start node, and Kruskal's sorts edges and adds those that join separate components.

children.title: Reconstruct Itinerary
children.description: Use every ticket exactly once, visiting airports in lexical order. Hierholzer's algorithm builds the path in reverse.

children.title: Choosing a shortest-path algorithm
children.description: BFS for unit weights, Dijkstra for non-negative weights, and Bellman-Ford for negative weights or hop limits.

leetcode-patterns.title: Dynamic Programming Patterns I: 1D and Knapsack
leetcode-patterns.description: Drill the first DP families. You will define state and transition, then convert a recursive solution to memoized and tabulated forms.
topics: Climbing Stairs and House Robber I and II
Coin Change and Coin Change II
leetcode-patterns.challenge: Solve 10 problems. For each, write the state, the transition and the base case before you code.

children.title: Climbing Stairs and House Robber
children.description: The answer at position i depends on one or two earlier answers. Keep only those and use constant space.

children.title: House Robber II
children.description: With a circular street, solve two linear cases: skip the first house, or skip the last, and take the better.

children.title: Coin Change and Coin Change II
children.description: The first asks for the fewest coins, the second for the number of ways. Loop order controls whether order matters.

children.title: Partition Equal Subset Sum
children.description: Reduce to a 0/1 knapsack: can a subset reach half the total? Iterate the sums backward to use each item once.

children.title: Longest Increasing Subsequence
children.description: A table of the best length ending at each index is quadratic. Patience sorting with binary search gets n log n.

children.title: Maximum Product Subarray
children.description: Track both the maximum and minimum product ending here, because a negative can flip them.

children.title: Word Break and Decode Ways
children.description: Ask whether a prefix can be formed from a valid piece plus a valid shorter prefix. Fill the table left to right.

children.title: Defining the state
children.description: Write what dp[i] means in one sentence before coding. A clear state makes the recurrence easy to see.

leetcode-patterns.title: Dynamic Programming Patterns II: 2D and Strings
leetcode-patterns.description: Drill grid and string DP. You will build tables for paths, subsequences and edit costs, and reduce space where possible.
topics: Unique Paths and Minimum Path Sum
leetcode-patterns.challenge: Solve 8 problems. Redo two of them with O(n) space and explain what you dropped.

children.title: Unique Paths and Minimum Path Sum
children.description: Each cell depends on the cell above and the one to the left. A single row of storage is enough.

children.title: Grid DP with obstacles
children.description: Set blocked cells to zero ways or infinite cost, and watch the first row and column carefully.

resources.label: Tech Interview Handbook - Coding interview study plan

children.title: Longest Common Subsequence
children.description: Compare the ends of both strings. If they match, extend the diagonal; otherwise take the better of dropping one character.

children.title: Edit Distance
children.description: Insert, delete or replace costs one each. The table cell takes the minimum of its three neighbors plus the right cost.

children.title: Longest Palindromic Substring
children.description: Expand around each center, for odd and even lengths, in quadratic time. A DP table works too.

children.title: Choosing expansion or a table
children.description: Expansion uses less memory and is simple. A table helps when you need many palindrome queries.

children.title: Interleaving String and Distinct Subsequences
children.description: Both use a table indexed by how much of each string is consumed. Define each cell as a yes/no or a count.

children.title: Regular Expression Matching
children.description: Handle the star by either skipping its pattern part or using it to match one more character. Memoize on both indexes.

children.title: Non-overlapping Intervals and Meeting Rooms II
children.description: Sort by end to keep the most intervals. For rooms, sweep sorted starts and ends or use a min-heap of end times.

children.description: Track the farthest reachable index. For the minimum jumps, treat each jump as a level in a BFS over ranges.

children.title: Gas Station and Partition Labels
children.description: A running total that never recovers tells you where to restart. For labels, extend the current part to the last occurrence.

children.title: Single Number and Number of 1 Bits
children.description: XOR cancels equal values, so duplicates vanish. Clear the lowest set bit with n and n-1 to count bits.

children.title: Bit tricks
children.description: Know shifts, masks, and, or, xor. A few identities solve many problems in constant space.

children.title: Reverse Integer
children.description: Build the result digit by digit and check for overflow before each multiply. Say how you handle the limits.

children.title: Pow(x, n)
children.description: Square the base and halve the exponent to get logarithmic time. Handle negative exponents and the minimum integer.

children.title: Setting up a timed round
children.description: Practice with a timer and no hints. 45 minutes for one medium, or 25 for each of two, matches a real round.
